title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
This incident is an impersonation fraud in which AI-generated images and videos of a real, named attorney were used to create hundreds of fake social media profiles advertising fictitious immigration services. The failure did not originate inside a legitimate AI product deployment; it is a case of AI tools being used offensively, outside any sanctioned system, to fabricate a credible professional identity at scale. The volume of fake profiles, nearly 6,500 removed across TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram, shows that platform-level detection did not catch the content before victims were harmed.

The harm landed on immigrants seeking legal help, who paid cash through peer-to-peer payment apps after receiving fake contracts. The conditions that allowed the scheme to persist were the ease of generating convincing likeness content, the speed at which fake profiles can be created across multiple platforms, and the absence of effective automated or human review that would flag coordinated impersonation of a specific real person before victims made contact.

What is not established is who is responsible, how many people lost money, whether any investigation has produced findings, and whether the platforms violated their own policies or any law. The reporting describes the harm and the attorney's response; it does not constitute proof of any specific actor's guilt or a determination of legal liability.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
# Summary

Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of an artificial intelligence scam targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake videos and social media profiles using AI-generated images of Leal to promote fraudulent immigration services, including offering US residency for $2,200 cash payments. The scams typically direct victims to contact phone numbers through WhatsApp, where fraudsters send fake contracts and collect payment through digital payment apps like Venmo, Zelle, and Cash App.

Leal first discovered the scheme in October when potential clients began calling his office, but the situation has dramatically worsened in recent months. His firm hired an anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. Leal has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the fraud. He advises immigrants to verify identities of legal service providers online and avoid anyone requesting immediate payments through digital apps.
